# Sheet

A panel that slides in from an edge.

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Record details beside the table.

- **Use it when:** Filters, details or a secondary form while the page stays in view.
- **Not when:** A blocking decision (dialog), or a tiny confirmation.

Instead:

- [Dialog](./dialog.md): A centered blocking window.
- [Drawer](./drawer.md): The bottom panel for phones.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A menu or dialog</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> elevation.overlay and a dimmed page for dialogs</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A border only</div></div><div class="cap">Floating things need a shadow so they read as on top.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add sheet
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
